title: Daily SGS Top 5
tagline: Five stories, one question: who's in control?

stories.headline: Bangladesh garment workers shut factories over pay
stories.summary: Garment workers in Bangladesh shut factories that supply big clothing brands, marching for wages more than double the current floor. Protests turned violent in several hubs.
stories.label: Slightly Sovereign
stories.why: Workers press bosses and their own government over pay.
stories.what_it_means: Workers are pressing bosses and their own government over pay.
stories.economic_impact: Hundreds of plants closed, and shipments risk delay.
stories.everyday_example: It's like the shop floor walking out until the register pays a living wage.

stories.headline: Paraguay impeaches Peña; Alliana sworn in
stories.summary: Paraguay's Senate removed Santiago Peña and swore in Pedro Alliana after the Ueno Bank collapse. Peña was placed under house arrest.
stories.label: Moderately Sovereign
stories.why: Lawmakers finish the accountability path they started when they refused his resignation.
stories.what_it_means: Lawmakers finished the accountability path they started when they refused his resignation.
stories.economic_impact: About three million depositors still wait on frozen savings.
stories.everyday_example: It's like the board firing the CEO after the credit union locked every card.

stories.headline: Russia upgrades its team for Abu Dhabi Ukraine talks
stories.summary: Russia named a senior team, led by Vladimir Medinsky, for US-mediated Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi. Deal terms are still undisclosed.
stories.label: Moderately Globalist
stories.why: Great-power rooms keep sketching Europe's next map while Ukrainians aren't holding the pen.
stories.what_it_means: Great-power rooms keep sketching Europe's next map while Ukrainians aren't holding the pen.
stories.economic_impact: Ceasefire odds and winter energy risk will move markets.
stories.everyday_example: It's like upgrading the landlords at the lease table while tenants wait outside.

stories.headline: US launches Task Force Iron Gate on Iran's land routes
stories.summary: US Central Command launched Task Force Iron Gate, about twenty people in Tampa, to disrupt Iran's land and Caspian routes for weapons and sanctioned goods. It adds to the naval blockade.
stories.label: Moderately Sovereign
stories.why: Washington chokes the overland paths Iran uses to restock.
stories.what_it_means: Washington is choking the overland paths Iran uses to restock.
stories.economic_impact: Centcom says the sea blockade has blocked over twenty-five billion in Iranian crude.
stories.everyday_example: It's like locking the alley after blocking the front gate.

stories.headline: Iran lifts missile range limit; Hormuz stays gated
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it lifted its two-thousand-kilometer missile range limit. An army spokesman said Hormuz stays gated until the US meets Tehran's demands. Whether longer-range missiles are already fielded is not independently verified.
stories.label: Strongly Globalist
stories.why: Iran uses a shared energy lane as leverage over other nations and fuel buyers.
stories.what_it_means: Iran is using a shared energy lane as leverage over other nations and fuel buyers.
stories.everyday_example: It's like a neighbor mining the only road and opening the gate on his terms.
